metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated system tray → Settings → Bluetooth. Desktop shows default light appearance. GNOME Settings sidebar visible with Appearance panel.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GNOME Settings sidebar panels (Appearance is directly visible in the Settings sidebar from the trajectory).
metadata.explanation: The screenshot shows 'Appearance' in the Settings sidebar (step 3 screenshot). Default color-scheme is 'default' (light). Evaluator checks gsettings 'color-scheme' contains 'prefer-dark' after the agent switches to dark mode.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly runs 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme' which directly reads the GNOME color scheme setting — the authoritative source for dark mode state.

Metric 'check_include_exclude' correctly receives the rules dict (include/exclude) as its second parameter when expected.type='rule', and accesses 'include'/'exclude' keys directly — no parameter handling error.

Expected value 'prefer-dark' is the correct gsettings value set when GNOME Dark mode is enabled. The command output is ''prefer-dark'' (with surrounding quotes), which contains the substring 'prefer-dark', so the include check passes correctly.
No postconfig needed: gsettings reads from dconf backend which is always accessible regardless of UI state.
Negative-control resistance confirmed: default color-scheme value is 'default' or 'prefer-light', which do not contain 'prefer-dark', so the initial state will not pass.
Full instruction coverage: the single requirement (switch to Dark mode) is completely verified by this one gsettings check.
